title: Rufus King (London) to the Secretary of State, 1797-1803 (NARA RG 59, M30 rolls 4-8): King's State Department code (the = 769) rebuilt from the Department's interlinear decipherments and tested on No. 59; No. 29 of 13 April 1797, on Sweden, read in part

steps.what: NARA OCR of M30 rolls 4-8 searched for runs of code groups (170 frames); 106 frames downloaded and classed: 57 coded despatch copies, 48 interlined by the Department's clerks, 9 bare (4 with no clear text on the film: No. 29, No. 30 triplicate, 25 Apr 1801 duplicate, 8 Jun 1801 run).

Identified the code: the = 769, of = 1410, to = 644 from King's first coded despatch (14 Jan 1797) to No. 89 (2 Apr 1803); not the 663 code and not any of Weber's nine 1600/1700 tables (40 values tested).
No. 59 (23 Dec 1797, 297 bare groups) transcribed without a key and set aside; the test declared and timestamped (19:43 -0500) before any interlined batch came back.
72 interlined frames of rolls 4-8 transcribed by seven agents with no key in view: 13,603 groups in 8,459 word rows (corpus/interlined_spans.tsv).

Key v1: 411 single-group values from the clerks' words (majority, ties left out) and 312 values from a frame solver that splits every multi-group word into elements of the printed 1600-element list; 723 groups, hashed.

Declared held-out test on No. 59 against the Department's clear text: 0.946 of 224 covered groups in order (coverage 0.742); 200 shuffled keys mean 0.108, best 0.165; pass rule (>= 0.85, margin >= 0.30) met. One run.
Bare items transcribed blind (No. 29, No. 30 triplicate, 25 Apr 1801 duplicate, 8 Jun 1801 run; 541 groups).

Key v1 applied to No. 30 and the 1801 items against King's printed texts (Life 2:172-75, 3:436-38, 472-73), not declared in advance: every code group laid in order on the letters of the print's italic runs, a group agreeing when it takes exactly its key value; 201 of 227, 85 of 100 and 9 of 9 covered groups agree (0.885, 0.85, 1.0); 1,000 permuted keys mean 0.094, 0.083, 0.043, best 0.181, 0.21, 0.222. scripts/check_against_print.py, fixed seed; replaces earlier figures (0.833, 0.81, 9/9) whose truth was the whole printed letter.
Key v2: 24 values aligned to the clear texts of No. 59, No. 30 and the 1801 items; calibration with a tenth of the key hidden: 92 of 94 proposed values right.

No. 29 decoded and read; places that did not read checked against the clerks' multi-group words: six D values corrected (1097 pre, 926 er, 246 pro, 1338 dec, 287 li, 128 m) and nine values added (986 reg, 587 par, 548 ty, 1209 nature, 461 ap, 1210 ne, 29 s, 1407 ite, 206 un); 1051 (Stockholm) re-read on the frame. Eight values left from context only, marked [?].

No. 29's clear pages transcribed in full from frames 0092 R to 0096 R (King's signature), two passes; no code on 0093-0096 and none on the enclosures to 0104; the clear words of the coded paragraph agree with the first transcription.

Prior art: Weber 1979, Tomokiyo's Cryptiana, Madison Papers, King's Life vols. 2-4, ASP FR 1-2, Founders Online, DECODE, this repository: no key of the 769 code; No. 29 not found in print. Weber assigns a King to Pickering letter of 13 Apr 1797 to WE025 (Adams Papers reel 392): not this code; that copy not seen.

Integration check by the project (pull request #398): key v1, the No. 59 score, key v2 and the print checks rebuilt byte for byte from the corpus; No. 59, No. 29 and No. 30 confirmed absent from the 72 corpus frames; frame 0092 fetched from NARA and all 119 groups read again with the transcription in view (all stand); the eight context-only groups searched in the corpus and the bare items (no occurrence under a clear word); key.tsv compared with Codes 10 and 16 (legation1788; Code 16 is in pinckney1793 since the split of 11 Nov 2026) and the WE028 sheet (morris1813): no value shared. The time of the test declaration rests on the contributor's statement (single commit).

Follow-up by Andrew Beling (PR #413), verified and integrated: in corpus/interlined_spans.tsv 769 stands alone under a clerk's word 465 times, 453 as 'the' and never as 'and'; 710 is 'and' or '&' 164 of 168 times and never 'the'; so the 769 of No. 29 line 15 has no parallel, and with one copy on the film it cannot be told whose slip it was. 269 found a second time under an interlined 'the' on M30 roll 6 frame 0013 (10 Jan 1799); on the frame the first digit could be 2 or a corrected 7, so it stays grade I. key.tsv row for 269 corrected (n 2, second sighting doubtful). No reading changes.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the State Department clerks' interlinear decipherments of King's other coded despatches on the same microfilm (72 frames), tested once on a held-out bare despatch (No. 59) against the Department's clear copy, and applied to No. 29, which has no decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_no29.md: decoded words only, 76 words with 11 holes (the ten context-only words marked [?word] and one supplied letter, overtur[e]); 0.994 over the whole despatch's reading with its clear words, frames 0092-0096 (research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.py share).

validation.notes: Contributor's declared held-out test (test_no59/PREREGISTRATION.md, not docs/_validate.py): key v1 (sha256 6a9a1d8c...9f064, 723 groups) on No. 59 against the Department's clear text; 0.946 of covered groups in order, coverage 0.742, 200 shuffled keys best 0.165; thresholds 0.85 and 0.30 fixed in advance. Reproduced byte for byte by scripts/king_code.py on 11 Nov 2026, by the contributor and again by the project on integration.

texts.label: No. 29, London, 13 Apr 1797 (M30 roll 4 frames 0092-0096; code on 0092)
texts.summary: King reports on Sweden: under the late regency (Duke Karl's guardianship, which ended when Gustav IV Adolf took over the government on 1 Nov 1796; Svenskt biografiskt lexikon, 'Gustav IV Adolf') Swedish policy favoured France; the young King is more national in outlook and French influence at Stockholm is less, so the President's answer to the Swedish overtures, declining them 'for the present', should be well received there. The overture is the Swedish minister Engeström's proposition to Thomas Pinckney, which Pickering answered through King on 17 Sept 1796 (Pickering to John Adams, 24 Sept 1798, Founders Online, Adams Papers 99-02-02-3023). The despatch then turns, in clear, to the Maryland Bank Stock, Captain Home and seamen.
texts.note: read_share 0.994 is measured over the whole despatch, whose clear pages (frames 0093-0096) are now transcribed; on the decoded words of the coded paragraph alone it is 0.855 (65 of 76). Marked read in part: ten coded words rest on this letter's context alone and are marked [?word].

reading_review.note: Read as sentences against frame 0092; signed off, including the ten context-only words (marked [?word]) and the supposed encoder's slip (769 for 'and'). On integration (11 Nov 2026) the project read it again as sentences against no29_decryption.txt and frame 0092: coherent English, the ten marked words and the supplied letter its only holes.

texts.label: No. 59, London, 23 Dec 1797 (M30 roll 4 frames 0272-0273): the held-out test
texts.summary: King reports that the British Cabinet has rejected a French peace proposal made through Talleyrand, the price of which was a bribe of a million sterling to the Directors, ministers and others; he vouches for the information but asks that it not be published as coming from him.
texts.note: Test document: its text is the Department's clear copy (contemporary); the decryption shows the frozen key's decode (V1) and key.tsv (K, not a test). Not claimed as a reading.

outcome.notes: Contributed by Andrew Beling (with AI agents). The key is new; most of King's coded despatches are in print (Life and Correspondence), so the texts are not, except No. 29, not found in print. Related: ../king1801 (closed 26 Oct 2026 as already in print), whose coded duplicates are on M30 roll 7 frames 0142 and 0162, not roll 9 (NOTES.md, 'For king1801'). key.tsv = build/key_v2.tsv plus 15 R and 8 I rows of 11 Nov 2026. Integration (11 Nov 2026): rebuild, test and print checks reproduced; the key's unvalued groups, the unopened frames, Pickering's instruction of 17 Sept 1796 and the lack of a blind second transcription are recorded in NOTES.md under 'Further work', not as gaps in the reading of No. 29.

prior.where: The key: none found (Weber 1979 no table; Tomokiyo's Cryptiana has no 769 = the; Madison Papers 'key not found'; ../king1801 'not identified or rebuilt'; DECODE no record). The texts: most of King's coded despatches are printed from his press copies in C. R. King, Life and Correspondence of Rufus King vols. 2-4 (1894-1900), coded words in italics (used here for No. 30 and the 1801 checks). No. 29 was not found in print (Life vol. 2, ASP FR 1-2, Founders Online); King's letterbooks, the Pickering Papers and Adams Papers reel 392 were not checked.

human: Andrew Beling set the task and the rules (blind transcription, a held-out test declared before the batches came back, every context-only value marked) and ran the agents; AI agents surveyed the film, transcribed, built and tested the key, aligned the clear texts, read No. 29 and searched the prior art. No human palaeographic check.
